name: Timothy Griffin
abstract_title: Criminal Justice and the Science of Consciousness: Quantification of a Distorted Discourse and the Case for "Heuristic Hooks"
abstract: Abstract A criminal justice professor argues that the increasingly advanced science of consciousness—especially neuroscientific findings on the neural correlates of agency—has profound implications for popular discourse on crime and justice policy. By challenging common psychological assumptions of conscious free will as the causal driver of behavior, these frameworks question foundational doctrines of culpability, mens rea, voluntary action, and retributivist punishment.
